findings.highlight: two, separated, become a pair of ones
findings.evidenceJa: 二人から一人が去り、一人と一人が残されてしまった
findings.explanation: The source says that one person leaves from the existing pair, after which two isolated individuals are left behind. The English turns that into the two simply separating into a pair of ones, obscuring both the departure and who remains.
findings.japanese:
二人から一人が去り、
一人と一人が残されてしまった日にも。
findings.todokanai: Falling on the day when two, separated, become a pair of ones.

findings.highlight: "She" is gone now. And only "she and I" remain.
findings.evidenceJa: 『あいつ』は去った。そして、『俺とあの娘』だけが残った。
findings.explanation: The Japanese pointedly gives Kazusa and Setsuna different marked labels: 'that one' leaves, while 'the girl and I' remain. Todokanai TL renders both women as the identical quoted 'she,' erasing the hierarchy and making the quotation marks meaningless.
findings.japanese:
『あいつ』は去った。
そして、『俺とあの娘』だけが残った。
findings.todokanai: "She" is gone now. And only "she and I" remain.

findings.highlight: I can't bring myself to turn around
findings.explanation: Haruki says he does not even turn his gaze back to her. “Can't bring myself to” changes deliberate nonresponse into emotional inability, weakening the self-accusation that continues into the following lines.
findings.japanese:
空を見上げた視線を、
声の主に戻すことすらしない。
findings.todokanai: Fixing my gaze toward the sky, I can't bring myself to turn around for the person calling out to me.

findings.highlight: I can't even bring myself to apologize
findings.explanation: Again, the source says he does not even apologize; it does not say that he is unable to. The mistranslation softens the cold behavior Haruki is deliberately condemning in himself.
findings.japanese:
そして、そんな突き放した態度を、
謝ることすらしない。
findings.todokanai: I can't even bring myself to apologize for being so callous to her.

findings.highlight: It wouldn't be right not to see my despicable actions to their very end.
findings.evidenceJa: 一度、最低の裏切りをしてしまった相手だから。もう、ずっと最低を貫かなくちゃならないから。
findings.explanation: Haruki repeats 最低 and turns his first betrayal into a self-imposed obligation to remain the worst. Todokanai TL replaces that repeated identity with plural 'despicable actions' and invents the moralizing claim that abandoning them 'wouldn't be right.'
findings.japanese:
一度、最低の裏切りをしてしまった相手だから。
もう、ずっと最低を貫かなくちゃならないから。
findings.todokanai: I've already committed the most despicable act of betrayal against her, after all. It wouldn't be right not to see my despicable actions to their very end.

findings.explanation: 柔らかさ is physical softness felt against Haruki's back, paired with warmth. “Gentle” turns the tactile detail into an abstract emotional quality.
findings.japanese: 背中に感じる柔らかさと温かさ。
findings.todokanai: Against my back, I feel a gentle and warm sensation.

findings.highlight: and if it's just causing you to suffer more
findings.evidenceJa: あのコを裏切ってしまうって、辛く感じるなら
findings.explanation: The second condition is specifically whether he finds the prospect of betraying her painful. The English invents a separate third condition about the embrace causing additional suffering.
findings.japanese:
「こうされることが嫌なら…
あのコを裏切ってしまうって、辛く感じるなら…」
findings.todokanai: "If you don't want this… if you think this means betraying her, and if it's just causing you to suffer more…"

findings.evidenceJa: あなたがわたしを受け入れてるって
findings.explanation: 受け入れてる describes the acceptance Setsuna might read into Haruki's present failure to reject her. “You'll come to accept me” moves that acceptance into the future. The separate scope of 悲しさのあまり is genuinely ambiguous and is not claimed as an error here.
findings.japanese:
「悲しさのあまり、あなたがわたしを受け入れてるって、
最低の思い込み、しちゃうよ？」
findings.todokanai: "I'll end up making the worst possible assumptionーthat, overwhelmed by sadness, you'll come to accept me, you know that?"

findings.highlight: "she" is the only thing on my mind right now
findings.evidenceJa: そんな瞬間も、俺の頭の中を占めているのが、『あいつ』のことしかないって事実に。
findings.explanation: The quoted 『あいつ』 deliberately recalls Haruki's marked designation of Kazusa at line 20. Rendering it as generic quoted 'she' removes the echo and the contrast with Setsuna, even as Setsuna is holding him.
findings.japanese:
そんな瞬間も、俺の頭の中を占めているのが、
『あいつ』のことしかないって事実に。
findings.todokanai: Even at this very moment… I can't deny the truth that "she" is the only thing on my mind right now.

findings.highlight: leaving us there in its wake
findings.evidenceJa: 俺たちを、そこに置き去りにしてくれる
findings.explanation: The snow spreads a white world before them and leaves them stranded there inside it. An expanding world cannot leave them “in its wake”; the image is defective English and reverses the spatial relation.
findings.japanese:
ただ白く、綺麗なだけの世界を目の前に広げ、
俺たちを、そこに置き去りにしてくれる。
findings.todokanai: A white world abundant only in beauty expands before our eyes, leaving us there in its wake.

findings.highlight: forgotten emotions it had been hiding
findings.evidenceJa: そうやって隠していた事実を、忘れていた想いを
findings.explanation: The source distinguishes facts concealed by the snow from feelings Haruki had forgotten. The English makes the snow the thing that had also been hiding the forgotten emotions, collapsing the contrast.
findings.japanese:
一度解けたら、そうやって隠していた事実を、
忘れていた想いを、もう一度白日の下にさらす。
findings.todokanai: Once it melts, all of the hidden truths and forgotten emotions it had been hiding will once again be brought into daylight for all to see.
